title: runtime(scheduler): two-queue dispatch policy for mixed short/long prompts + aging guardrails
author: Marcus Reed
description: Context: mixed prompt-length workloads (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context requests) can produce head-of-line blocking in continuous batching, inflating p95/TTFT for latency-sensitive traffic. This PR introduces a two-queue dispatch policy (short/long classes) with explicit starvation prevention via aging + bounded skew, behind a feature flag, and adds basic correctness tests plus perf notes from local mixed-load runs. The classification logic lands in pr-24831; this PR assumes requests arrive with a class label and focuses on dispatch selection + guardrails.
body: What changed: implemented a class-based scheduler policy with two logical queues (SHORT, LONG) and a dispatch loop that chooses the next request to admit into the next prefill/decode iteration. The policy biases toward SHORT to reduce user-visible tail latency under mixed workloads, while guaranteeing progress for LONG via (1) aging that increases LONG priority as time-in-queue grows and (2) a max-skew guardrail to prevent unbounded short dominance. Design summary: The scheduler maintains per-class queues and per-class accounting over a rolling window. On each dispatch tick, we compute an effective priority for each class based on (base weight * backlog signal) plus an aging boost derived from the head-of-queue waiting time; we then select the class with higher effective priority, subject to a max-consecutive-short limit and a minimum long share floor when long backlog exists. The chosen request is then fed into existing batch formation, with minimal structural changes to avoid destabilizing kernel selection. Starvation prevention: (a) aging_half_life_ms controls how quickly LONG priority rises with wait time; (b) max_short_burst caps consecutive SHORT selections when LONG backlog is non-empty; (c) long_force_after_ms forces a LONG selection when the oldest LONG exceeds a hard wait threshold; and (d) queue-level invariants are asserted in debug builds and covered by unit tests. Feature flag/config: gated behind runtime.scheduler.policy = two_queue (default remains legacy), with knobs runtime.scheduler.two_queue.short_weight, long_weight, aging_half_life_ms, max_short_burst, long_force_after_ms, and max_dispatch_skew_ratio (validated and clamped to safe bounds). Tests: added deterministic scheduler unit tests for (1) no starvation under sustained short arrival (long eventually dispatches), (2) short preference when both queues non-empty and long age is low, (3) hard force trigger when oldest long exceeds threshold, and (4) stability of selection under jittery arrival patterns. Perf notes (local/dev bench): using a synthetic 80/20 short/long mix with long prompts ~8k context and short ~256 tokens on A100-80GB dev host, observed reduced p95 queue wait for short requests vs legacy policy with negligible throughput drift in steady state; results are directional only (real validation in benchmark-lab + perf-canary will follow in separate PRs). Follow-ups: token-budget guardrails and per-class metrics/tracing are intentionally not included here to keep review scope focused (see pr-24872 and pr-24888). Risk/rollback: fully gated; can revert to legacy by config. Known risks are parameter sensitivity and pathological mixes; addressed partially via bounded skew + hard force and covered by correctness tests. Pseudocode sketch (for reviewer orientation, not exact code): selectClass(): if longQ empty -> SHORT; if shortQ empty -> LONG; if oldestLongWait > long_force_after_ms -> LONG; if consecutiveShort >= max_short_burst -> LONG; scoreShort = short_weight * f(backlogShort); scoreLong = long_weight * f(backlogLong) + agingBoost(oldestLongWait, aging_half_life_ms); if scoreShort/scoreLong > max_dispatch_skew_ratio -> LONG else choose argmax(scoreShort, scoreLong).

scheduler: add aging + max burst guardrails; clamp config bounds

docs(dev): add perf notes + debug logging for class selection (guarded)
review_conversation: Lena Fischer (review): Can you clarify the starvation guarantee? Specifically, what prevents long from starving if short arrival is sustained and short_weight is high? Also request: add a regression test that simulates a constant short stream with a single long enqueued at t=0 and asserts long dispatches within bounded steps/time.

Marcus Reed (author): Added long_force_after_ms + max_short_burst enforcement when long backlog is non-empty. Also added test_two_queue_policy.no_starvation_under_sustained_short to assert long dispatch occurs within N selections; wired test to virtual clock so it’s deterministic.

Sofia Ivanova (review): The max_dispatch_skew_ratio logic reads like it compares class scores directly, but scores can be near-zero when backlog is small. Please add comments/guards for divide-by-zero and document how f(backlog) behaves (linear vs log). Also: ensure legacy policy remains default for all pools until canary.

Marcus Reed (author): Updated scoring to avoid division by zero (epsilon floor) and added inline comment explaining backlog transform (log1p to reduce sensitivity). Confirmed default remains legacy; two_queue requires explicit config/flag.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Concern: picking class first and then letting batch formation run could still allow long-prefill to dominate if we admit a long with huge prefill cost. Are we separating prefill vs decode selection here?

Marcus Reed (author): This PR only gates the admission decision; prefill/decode separation hooks are being refactored in pr-24857 to avoid long-prefill dominating batch selection. Added a note in docs + TODO in dispatcher to keep reviewers aligned.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Please be careful with changes that might increase sequence-length variance within a batch and destabilize kernel selection. Any changes to batch composition beyond class selection?

Marcus Reed (author): No direct changes to batch composition; we select the next request class and then defer to existing batch builder constraints. Added debug counters to log when class selection results in large variance (guarded; metrics will come later).

Sean Gallagher (review): Add explicit rollback guidance in the PR description and ensure the policy can be toggled without restart (config reload path). Also: please link the SLO guardrails doc and call out canary-only usage.

Marcus Reed (author): Confirmed config reload supports policy knob changes at runtime; added note: rollback by setting runtime.scheduler.policy=legacy. Linked SUP-19387 context and referenced the SLO guardrails doc in internal notes.
